LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 9.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one

Strand: My Friends Suggested vocabulary kind, caring, loving, funny, friendly, close, pl
Topic 9.1: Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of My Friends Suggested vocabulary kind, caring, loving, funny, friendly, close, pl in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why should we say sounds and words correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 9.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn- Learning independently is enhanced as they get motivated to perfect the pronunciation of various sounds.

● Digital literacy- Learner’s ability to interact with technology is enhanced as they listen to an audio recording and mimic the sounds.

Values:
Unity: Cooperation is enhanced as they collaborate with each other as they sing and recite poems related to friends.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Self-awareness – Learner’s self –awareness is nurtured as they acquire knowledge about their friends.

Link to other Learning Areas

The learners uses the acquired pronunciation skills to express themselves fully when learning concept in other all learning areas.

Suggested learning resources

• Audio recording,

• Braille charts,

• Songs,

• Textbooks in print and in braille
